sampling: 285 blank-line paragraphs after front matter (fenced blocks kept whole); paragraphs 1,4,7,...,283 (every third from 1); claims drawn from those paragraphs

score_evidence.A: Headings are claim noun phrases with no skipped levels, tables and fences render, $$ math only (L775-L779), use_math true. Deductions: the quickstart '도구 두 개로 끝나는 첫 에이전트' sits at L530, after the hook, middleware and intervention sections whose code already uses letter_counter/file_editor (L232 '앞서 만든 글자 세기 에이전트의 letter_counter, file_editor', L294 '# letter_counter: 앞서 정의한 글자 세기 도구', L478 '빠른 시작에서 letter_counter와 file_editor를 정의한 스크립트에 이어 붙이는'); the install commands appear inside the hook-retry subsection (L164-L169) instead of the quickstart; description is 101 characters (blog spec 120-160).
score_evidence.B: Mostly natural '입니다' prose with varied sentence shapes. Deductions: L53 '이 루프를 짜는 사람은 개발자가 아닙니다. 모델은 `Agent`에 넘기는 객체 하나일 뿐이고' (confusing subject; rewrite '루프는 개발자가 짜지 않습니다. 모델 객체를 Agent에 넘기면 에이전트가 ...'); L575 '이는 서드파티 블로그 AWS SDK Masterclass의 모범 사례입니다' (rewrite '이 권고는 서드파티 블로그 AWS SDK Masterclass가 제시합니다'); L144 '정리한 것으로' noun frame; formulaic '다음과 같습니다' x5 and L132 '표로 옮기면 이렇습니다'; L65 '누적 구조가 이 순서를 가능하게 합니다' (English-shaped); 16 '할 수 있습니다'.
score_evidence.C: Forward references: three code blocks and their lead-ins point back to a quickstart that only appears at L530-L571. The running example is introduced twice in near-identical words (L39 and L57). L13 and L29 restate the same positioning ('오픈소스 SDK ... 호스팅되는 컨트롤 플레인 없이 ... 직접 에이전트 루프를 작성할 상황에서 대신'). Cross-references by section title (L891, L1115, L1216) are accurate.
score_evidence.D: Hard parts get worked examples where they appear: history growth table (L59-L65), end_turn cutting 3 model calls to 2 (L207, reproduced), middleware vs hook attempt visibility (L276-L278), Transform/Guide precedence table (L428-L435), 200,000 x 0.7 = 140,000 threshold (L779), 4,000 + 7,000 token overshoot (L816), the Guide-cap conflict with allowed actions (L495). Little padding.
score_evidence.E: Tables where comparison helps (stop reasons L79, writable properties L146, stages L255, actions L402/L412, retry params L619, checkpoints L838, outcome policy L824); event order and span tree as text diagrams (L109, L262, L1123), labelled as examples. No real loop or architecture figure; no image of the agent loop at all.
score_evidence.F: All 15 sampled claims are supported. Off-sample: L1212 credits the DEV Community customer-support article with 'Strands가 AWS용으로 설계되어 Amazon 내부에서 쓰이고 스트리밍과 병렬 에이전트를 지원한다며 프로덕션 준비도를 유망하게 평가' but the fetched article has no passage on internal Amazon use, streaming, parallel agents or a readiness verdict (search for 'intern', 'parallel', 'streaming', 'promising', 'readiness' finds nothing) -> unsupported attribution (-2). Minor imprecision: L489 '열 번째 호출까지는 ... FileEditApproval이 Confirm을 반환' holds only for file_editor calls.
score_evidence.T1: Every Python block runs against SDK 1.64.0 once the quickstart's letter_counter and file_editor are in scope: hooks (RetryOnToolError, EndAfterFileEdit -> 2 model calls), Input/Wrap middleware, approval_gate interrupt and resume (approved -> success, other -> error result), intervention handlers with Confirm/resume, StrictAuth fail-closed with the class-attribute on_error, retry strategy subclass/hook/middleware, both conversation managers, limits (turns=1 -> limit_turns), normalize_records cancel tool, handle_request, structured output (validation error fed back, then object), Cedar (bob denied, alice allowed), telemetry, create_harness. Deductions: blocks at L234, L288 and L480 rely on names defined later at L548; the Cedar block needs the strands-agents[cedar] extra (cedarpy), never mentioned; L1009 uses a placeholder model id.
score_evidence.T2: Covers what the sources cover in a sensible order (loop -> hooks -> middleware -> interventions -> quickstart -> retries -> context -> lifecycle limits -> structured output -> HITL -> traces -> choice). Only the quickstart is out of learning order.
score_evidence.T3: Explains mechanisms and why: hooks outside the middleware chain (L382-L392), reverse After ordering for cleanup symmetry (L130), precedence vs registration order (L424-L435), retry layering and stacking (L716-L718), limits checked at the top of iterations (L816), cooperative cancellation checkpoints (L838-L845), per-request agents vs idempotency (L893). Design advice is phrased as advice. Failure-mode section (L1214-L1218) is only pointers back.

examples.claim: Open-source SDK running in the user's process with no hosted control plane; ships turn limits, token budgets, cancellation, stop reasons
examples.source: strandsagents.com home: 'Strands runs inside your own process ... there is no hosted control plane'; Agent Loop intro lists invocation limits, cancellation, stop reasons (home page not in the Sources list).

examples.claim: limit_* stop reasons leave the message history valid; reinvoke with a larger budget or a different prompt
examples.source: Agent Loop: 'The agent's message history remains in a valid state, and you can reinvoke with a higher budget or different prompt.'

examples.claim: HookOrder.SDK_FIRST -100, DEFAULT 0 (implicit), SDK_LAST 100; not enforced bounds; float('-inf')/float('inf') for absolute ordering
examples.source: Hooks: 'HookOrder.SDK_FIRST (-100) ... DEFAULT (0): implicit when no order is specified ... SDK_LAST (100) ... These are not enforced bounds ... float('-inf')/float('inf') for guaranteed absolute ordering.'

examples.claim: On tool retry, ToolStreamEvents from discarded attempts were already emitted; only the final ToolResultEvent enters history
examples.source: Hooks: 'intermediate streaming events (ToolStreamEvent) from discarded attempts will have already been emitted ... Only the final attempt's ToolResultEvent is emitted and added to conversation history.'

examples.claim: AfterInvocationEvent.resume re-invokes with a string/content blocks/messages from BeforeInvocationEvent; in TypeScript it re-enters under the same invocation lock
examples.source: Hooks 'Invocation resume'; Hook events (TS): 'Setting it re-enters the agent loop under the same invocation lock.'

examples.claim: A Wrap middleware calling next three times sees all three attempts while Before/AfterModelCallEvent fire once
examples.source: Middleware: 'A retry produces one hook pair, not many. Middleware that calls next three times is invisible to hooks, which only see the outermost call and result.'

examples.claim: Guide in after_model_call retries the model with no framework cap; the docs' 'escalate to Deny' advice conflicts with after_model_call's allowed actions
examples.source: Interventions: 'The framework imposes no retry cap on guide-triggered retries' and 'escalating to Deny'; lifecycle table: after_model_call Proceed, Guide, Transform; Deny on after events 'No effect (warns at runtime)'.

examples.claim: on_error 'throw' default rethrows, 'proceed' fail-open, 'deny' logs and treats as Deny (fail-closed)
Default retry: up to 5 retries (6 attempts), 4 s first delay doubling; max_attempts 6, initial_delay 4, max_delay 128
examples.source: Retry Strategies: 'retry throttling errors up to 5 times (6 total attempts) with exponential backoff starting at 4 seconds'; parameter table 6 / 4 / 128.

examples.claim: proactive_compression=True uses threshold 0.7; with a 200,000-token limit compression fires at 140,000 projected tokens; best-effort, errors swallowed
examples.source: Conversation Management: 'Use True for the default 0.7 threshold ... 0.7 will trigger compression when 70% of the model's context window is used'; 'Proactive compression is best-effort only, so if reduce() throws or returns false, the error is swallowed'. 0.7 x 200,000 = 140,000.

examples.claim: Token limits count only this agent's model calls (not agents-as-tools or summarization); on Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini cache reads/writes count in full
examples.source: Agent Loop: 'Token limits count only this agent's own model calls ...'; 'On Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google Gemini, that total counts prompt-cache reads and writes in full'.

examples.claim: Python checks cancellation at four checkpoints (streaming, before tool, during MCP tool, after tool) with the listed behaviours
examples.source: Agent Loop: 'The agent checks for cancellation at four checkpoints' table (Python), rows and notes match.
Traces: export lines verbatim; comment 'Opt into the latest OTEL semantic conventions, and send tool definitions as spans.'

examples.claim: strands-harness needs Python 3.10+; TypeScript @strands-agents/harness needs Node.js 20+
examples.source: Harness quickstart: 'Requires Python 3.10 or newer.' / 'Requires Node.js 20 or newer.'
